task:
FIX CONSTRUCTION-POINT PORT COSTS AND COUNTING TO MATCH THE MEGA GUIDE (CRE CL-0013..CL-0024).

Context: apps/api/src/mechanics/cp_rules.py holds invented port-cost tables ([16,20,26,34,44,56] etc.; cp_simulator.py calls them "community estimates") and the simulator counts Tier 2 and Tier 3 ports separately. The source of truth is the Elite Dangerous Colonization Mega Guide v2.3.0, PDF pages 27-28 (text committed under docs/reference/colonisation/sources/mega-guide-v2.3.0/), already recorded in the CRE research repo as claims CL-0013..CL-0024 and rules CR-0010..CR-0012; see also docs/development/evidence/2026-10-21-cre-cpe-utilisation-audit.md row 7. This code is the base for the planned construction-point budget and port-order calculator (docs/ROADMAP.md owner decision D3, 2026-10-21). It is NOT used by Ratings V4, the published Finder products or apps/web; do not touch those.

Required behaviour:
1. ONE shared escalation count across Tier 2 and Tier 3 ports. Only escalating ports count. In cp_rules.py define ESCALATING_PORT_TIER_BY_ID = {coriolis_station: 2, asteroid_base: 2, orbis_t3: 3, ocellus_station: 3, dodecahedron_t3: 3, planetary_port: 3} (ids from apps/api/src/domain/facility_catalogue_v1.json) and NON_ESCALATING_PORT_IDS = the six space outposts (orbital_outpost_civilian, _commercial, _criminal, _industrial, _military, _scientific), the three planetary outposts (surface_planetary_port_outpost_civilian, _industrial, _scientific) and the six large settlements (surface_settlement_agriculture_t2_l, _extraction_t2_l, _industrial_t2_l, _military_t2_l, _research_bio_t2_l, _tourism_t2_l). The catalogue mislabels those 15 as Tier 2 ports; do NOT change catalogue tiers or the importer in this task. A non-escalating facility never advances the count and is charged its own catalogue yellow_cp_cost/green_cp_cost. For any facility id in neither set (test templates, the internal dummy ports used by cp_simulator.analyse_cp_budget), fall back to: is_port and tier in {2,3} means an escalating port of that tier. Put this classification in one small pure function in cp_rules.py and use it everywhere.
2. The primary port is exempt: it is charged nothing and does not advance the count (keep the existing primary-port note).
3. Cost of the nth counted port (n starts at 1): Tier 2 port = yellow max(3, 2n-1), i.e. 3,3,5,7,9,11..., green 0. Tier 3 port = green 6*max(1, n-1), i.e. 6,6,12,18,24,30..., yellow 0. Implement as small pure functions with named constants and a docstring citing "Mega Guide v2.3.0 PDF p27-28; CRE CL-0013..CL-0024, CR-0010..CR-0012". Remove T2_PORT_COSTS_YELLOW, T3_PORT_COSTS_YELLOW, T2_PORT_COSTS_GREEN, T3_PORT_COSTS_GREEN, the four *_EXTRAPOLATION_STEP constants, the _T*_PORT_COSTS_* aliases and every use of them. Rewrite the cp_simulator.py module docstring so it no longer says the curves are undocumented community estimates.
4. Record the known uncertainty in a code comment and as a note on the affected build-order timeline step: the guide's worked example on p28 (order T3,T3,T2,T2) totals 16 yellow while its own table gives 5+7=12; keep the table values and mark Tier 2 costs from the 3rd counted port onward as "guide table; guide example disagrees; not verified in-game". Also comment that dodecahedron_t3 is treated as Tier 3 like Orbis/Ocellus although guide v2.3.0 does not name it.
5. Apply the same rules everywhere costs are computed: simulation/build_order.py simulate_build_order (replace paid_t2/paid_t3 with the one shared counter; keep the t2_ports/t3_ports counts in the output), simulation/cp_simulator.py (port_cp_cost: change it to take the tier and the shared 1-based count and document that; CPState.place_port, next_t2_cost and next_t3_cost use the shared count; analyse_cp_budget may keep simulating T2-only and T3-only budgets), simulation/buildability.py _expected_yellow_need (sum the new Tier 2 costs for min(total_slots, 6) counted ports). The "Build T3 ports earlier to avoid later escalation" warning must fire only when a Tier 3 port is charged after at least one paid Tier 2 port. Leave LATE_T3_BUILD_ORDER_THRESHOLD and cp_repair.py alone unless a failing test proves they must change.
6. Do not change API response shapes, field names or OpenAPI output; do not edit facility_catalogue_v1.json, the importer, Ratings V4 files, shared_contracts/, sql/, apps/web/ or frontend/.

Tests (pytest, no database). Add tests/test_cp_escalation_guide.py using the bundled catalogue (edfinder_api.domain.facilities.load_bundled_catalogue) and simulate_build_order, with enough generated points that nothing is short, asserting for non-primary ports unless stated: (a) coriolis_station, asteroid_base, orbis_t3, ocellus_station spends 6 yellow and 30 green; (b) orbis_t3, ocellus_station, coriolis_station, asteroid_base spends 12 yellow and 12 green; (c) primary coriolis_station then coriolis_station spends 3 yellow; (d) primary orbis_t3 then ocellus_station, dodecahedron_t3, planetary_port, coriolis_station spends 24 green and 7 yellow; (e) coriolis_station, orbital_outpost_civilian, asteroid_base spends 6 yellow, the outpost costs 0 and gives 1 yellow; (f) each of the 9 outposts costs 0 and never advances the count, and each of the 6 large settlements costs 1 yellow, gives 2 green and never advances the count; (g) direct function tests: 6th counted Tier 2 port = 11 yellow, 6th counted Tier 3 port = 30 green; (h) a catalogue guard: every bundled entry with is_port and tier in {2,3} is in exactly one of ESCALATING_PORT_TIER_BY_ID or NON_ESCALATING_PORT_IDS, and every id in both sets exists in the bundled catalogue; (i) the "Build T3 ports earlier" warning appears for order (a), where Tier 3 ports are charged after paid Tier 2 ports, and does not appear for order (b).
Update existing tests that pin the old numbers so they assert the new contract (tests/test_simulation_preview.py test_cp_escalation_for_paid_t2_and_t3_ports becomes 3+3 yellow and 12 green with t2_ports 2 and t3_ports 1; test_primary_port_exemption_skips_first_escalating_cost becomes 3 yellow; plus any pins in tests/test_plan_ranker.py, tests/test_recommended_builds.py, tests/test_optimiser.py, tests/test_simulation_contract.py, tests/test_simulation_contracts.py). Never delete or weaken an assertion just to make it pass; if a test's intent no longer holds, say so in your summary. Run ruff on touched files and pytest on the new file plus every test file that imports cp_rules, cp_simulator, build_order, buildability or build_preview. In your summary list each changed number old -> new.
